21123525-f344-4423-9f74-a37604e29445._name: Associate Degree in Health [Exit Only Award]
21123525-f344-4423-9f74-a37604e29445.description: The Associate Degree in Health is an exit-only award for students who begin one of several University of Newcastle health degrees and need to leave before completing the full program. It sits at AQF level 6 and is available as an exit point from the Bachelor of Exercise and Sport Science, Bachelor of Midwifery, Bachelor of Nursing, Bachelor of Oral Health Therapy, or Bachelor of Podiatry. Students are not directly admitted to this award; it is only granted when a student exits one of these degrees early, and the qualification is conferred as an ordinary award rather than with honours.

7a429f56-cd64-4a57-be2a-0703d260aca0.description: The Associate Degree in Science is an exit-only award for students who complete two years of study in an associated Bachelor of Science program. It sits at AQF level 6 and gives students who need to leave their degree early, for example because of mitigating personal circumstances, a formal qualification to show for their study rather than no award at all. Students who later resolve the circumstances that led them to exit can return and complete the final year of their original Bachelor program.

35f70a59-6202-4e9f-a39e-c873b65da544.description: The Bachelor of Aboriginal Studies (Honours) is a one-year honours program for graduates of the Bachelor of Aboriginal Studies, Bachelor of Aboriginal Professional Practice, Bachelor of Global Indigenous Studies, Bachelor of Arts, or Bachelor of Social Science with a major in Aboriginal Studies or Global Indigenous Studies. Completed full time in one year or part time over a longer period, it is specifically Aboriginal in orientation and lets graduates deepen a particular area of interest, preparing them for roles such as service delivery within Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander organisations. International students from health, education, and social science backgrounds with a relevant degree are also encouraged to apply.

5df732c5-7abf-4c25-8b80-ecfbf032f4bd.description: The Bachelor of Biomedicine trains students in the structure and function of living organisms, with a particular focus on the human body. Combining this knowledge with problem-solving skills, critical reasoning, and scientific method, graduates are prepared to take part in scientific investigations of human structure and function in health and disease at the molecular, cellular, and whole-system level.

d6895e17-dc00-4665-9ecb-7720319335fc.description: The Bachelor of Computing (Honours) is an additional one-year program normally taken by students with a strong academic record in the Bachelor of Computer Science or Bachelor of Information Technology who want to broaden their knowledge before entering professional practice or applying for a research degree. Students complete a project course alongside further courses in research methods or advanced computing topics.

b102b418-706f-41e9-87d3-35de11e0ad21.description: Graduates of the Bachelor of Construction Management (Building) (Honours) move into leadership roles across the construction industry, including project management, contract management, estimating, quantity surveying, and property development, working on the delivery of buildings and infrastructure projects on site or in the office. The four-year program builds skills in building information modelling, building surveying, construction ecology and technology, health and safety, project management, procurement and tendering, quantity surveying, and sustainable development, and includes 12 weeks of career-ready placement. Employment in construction management remains strong, with building and construction employment nationally projected to grow from around 1.32 million jobs in 2024-25 to almost 1.5 million by 2029-30.

f972350b-139a-466e-8854-c39f2b068df7._name: Bachelor of Education (Early Childhood and Primary)
f972350b-139a-466e-8854-c39f2b068df7.description: The Bachelor of Education (Early Childhood and Primary) is a dual teaching qualification covering early childhood and primary education, preparing graduates to teach children from birth to 12 years old. The four-year program is offered at the Newcastle and Gosford campuses and leads most graduates into classroom teaching, though the qualification also opens up related careers in education leadership, research, and policy.

ef4f608a-5240-4db4-8f9b-ebd83d8b9630._name: Bachelor of Education Studies [Exit Only Award]
ef4f608a-5240-4db4-8f9b-ebd83d8b9630.description: The Bachelor of Education Studies is an exit-only award and does not qualify graduates to teach. It is available to students who begin a University of Newcastle teaching degree but need to leave before completing it, letting them graduate with developed problem-solving, communication, and critical thinking skills for education-related careers outside the classroom. Graduates of this award cannot be readmitted to, or complete, another teaching degree at the University of Newcastle.

ed725a1e-4bb5-4ba5-b1e4-b25faec7df4f._name: Bachelor of Exercise and Sports Science (Honours)
ed725a1e-4bb5-4ba5-b1e4-b25faec7df4f.description: The Bachelor of Exercise and Sport Science (Honours) is an additional year of study offered to graduates of the undergraduate program, completed full time in one year or part time over two years. Students complete a research project on a topic agreed with a research supervisor, alongside a skills strand that develops their research and thesis-writing abilities. The qualification is well regarded by employers and provides a pathway into a research career.

10aa028e-7f24-466e-8ed3-0e6716ae1421.description: The Bachelor of Health is an AQF level 7 exit-only award for students who need to leave one of several longer University of Newcastle health degrees before completing it, including the Bachelor of Medical Radiation Science (Honours) variants, Bachelor of Medicine, Bachelor of Nutrition and Dietetics (Honours), Bachelor of Occupational Therapy (Honours), Bachelor of Pharmacy (Honours), Bachelor of Physiotherapy (Honours), and Bachelor of Speech Pathology (Honours). It gives students a formal qualification to show for their study rather than no award at all, without directly admitting new students.

853541fc-8021-4371-8006-2ecfdcc28597.description: The Bachelor of Health Science (Honours) lets students build on an undergraduate Health Science degree with a further year of supervised research and presentation work, adding evidence to the body of undergraduate programs offered within Health Science. The program is in teach-out and no longer open to new students; it remains available only to students who commenced study before it closed to new admissions.

5dd708d2-dba9-4546-9386-5727d7f28ad0._name: Bachelor of Mechatronics Engineering (Honours)/B Electrical & Electronic Engineering (Honours)
5dd708d2-dba9-4546-9386-5727d7f28ad0.description: This double degree combines the Bachelor of Mechatronics Engineering (Honours) with the Bachelor of Electrical and Electronic Engineering (Honours). Mechatronics engineers work across a wide range of modern technologies, from robotics and vehicle optimisation to appliance design and biomechanics, including the design, automation, and operation of electro-mechanical systems. Electrical and electronic engineering applies mathematics, science, technology, and problem-solving to design, build, and maintain the products and services that underpin modern society. Together the two majors give graduates a broad engineering skill set spanning both disciplines.

d92fc2ee-ed15-4b55-a59c-ce480ae2f17d._name: Bachelor of Medical Radiation Science (Honours) (Diagnostic Radiography)
d92fc2ee-ed15-4b55-a59c-ce480ae2f17d.description: The Bachelor of Medical Radiation Science (Honours) (Diagnostic Radiography) prepares students for a career using advanced medical imaging technology, developing the clinical reasoning and patient management skills needed to create the medical images used to diagnose and manage patient health. The four-year program includes around 40 weeks of clinical placement, drawing on more than 30 years of experience training diagnostic radiographers, and graduates go on to work in private and public imaging departments, emergency wards, and operating theatres.

67954b96-07d1-44a1-90d7-998527c44f09.description: Foundation Studies, marketed as Open Foundation, is the University of Newcastle's free pathway into university for people without the entry requirements for direct admission, including school leavers, career changers, and those returning to study. On successful completion, students gain competitive entry into every degree at the University of Newcastle and access to the Guaranteed Admissions Scheme, which offers guaranteed entry into more than 70 selected degrees, along with access to the university's alumni community and its benefits.

a554e04f-a85f-4e48-afe3-294d32d71504._name: Graduate Certificate in Health Economics, Management and Policy
a554e04f-a85f-4e48-afe3-294d32d71504.description: The Graduate Certificate in Health Economics, Management and Policy develops skills in strategic health leadership and management, healthcare policy and governance, and health economics for health management professionals such as healthcare managers, policymakers, and analysts responding to challenges in the health sector. The program is in teach-out and no longer open to new students; it remains available only to students who commenced study before it closed to new admissions.

8c0b68d8-aca7-433c-b947-b69e9b6843f0.description: The Graduate Diploma in Laboratory Medicine is designed for graduates of biology, biotechnology, or biomedical science degrees who want a career in diagnostic pathology. Students gain hands-on experience with current advances in diagnostic medicine and develop the practical laboratory skills and advanced diagnostic techniques used in the field, preparing graduates for employment in a diagnostic pathology laboratory.

d914e327-8619-43b2-b220-336729e02a8b.description: The Master of Construction Management (Professional) is designed for graduates and industry professionals looking to move into project management and leadership roles in the built environment, with entry that recognises prior qualifications and industry experience. The two-year program, offered online or on campus, builds skills in project management, cost estimation, scheduling, and construction delivery, responding to building and construction employment that is nationally projected to grow from around 1.32 million jobs in 2024-25 to almost 1.5 million by 2029-30.

c689ea46-b5b5-4203-9046-fba79130f898._name: Master of Disaster Resilience and Sustainable Development
c689ea46-b5b5-4203-9046-fba79130f898.description: The Master of Disaster Resilience and Sustainable Development is built around the United Nations' 2030 Development Agenda and its Sustainable Development Goals, covering climate change, disaster risk reduction, and partnerships for development funding. The program focuses on disaster risk reduction and sustainable development, exposing students to the UN frameworks, tools, and metrics used to plan and manage resilient development strategies; graduates of courses that include UN-related tools and training also receive UN certification alongside their University of Newcastle testamur. The program is in teach-out and no longer open to new students.

7884f5dc-bb8c-4acf-b9b8-26863d05e8c0.description: The Master of Dispute Resolution is aimed at professionals who want to build their conflict resolution knowledge, skills, and career options through a multidisciplinary postgraduate coursework program. Graduates gain advanced knowledge and skills in dispute resolution that position them for further study, research, and professional practice in Australia and internationally. The program is in teach-out and no longer open to new students; it remains available only to students who commenced study before it closed to new admissions.

3e084b70-d3bf-4f9a-b23e-30fd7f102ce2._name: Master of Health Economics, Management and Policy
3e084b70-d3bf-4f9a-b23e-30fd7f102ce2.description: The Master of Health Economics, Management and Policy gives students a multidisciplinary skill set for addressing the challenges facing the healthcare industry, with the option to focus on health economics and policy, health management and leadership, health analytics and informatics, or research. The program is in teach-out and no longer open to new students; it remains available only to students who commenced study before it closed to new admissions.

32bbe743-97b6-4c7b-a047-2ff36118a8a7._name: Master of Leadership and Management in Education
32bbe743-97b6-4c7b-a047-2ff36118a8a7.description: The Master of Leadership and Management in Education exposes students to current research and practice in the leadership, management, and administration of educational institutions, with specialisations in People and Organisations, Quality Teaching and Pedagogy, Research and Evaluation, and Digital Learning and Innovation. Taught by experienced practitioners and active researchers, the program integrates theory and practice so graduates can apply current research to improve practice in their own workplace.

758f3d31-c41c-4310-9ad4-335af6187cd4._name: Master of Professional Engineering (Geospatial Engineering and Surveying)
758f3d31-c41c-4310-9ad4-335af6187cd4.description: The Master of Professional Engineering (Geospatial Engineering and Surveying) is designed for graduates looking to launch or advance a career in surveying and geospatial engineering, building management expertise alongside specialised technical skills for senior industry roles. The two-year program covers specialised spatial data collection, analysis, and management, with the option to broaden into a complementary area such as business, and includes 12 weeks of industrial experience across fields such as land surveying, mining surveying, remote sensing, geodesy, construction, and environmental management.

b13910ee-4473-4920-a5e9-37adbb5a9c4d.description: The Doctor of Philosophy (Medicine) is the University of Newcastle's research doctorate for candidates undertaking an original, supervised research project in medicine, run through the university's Graduate Research School rather than as a coursework program. Candidates work with a supervisory team within a School of the university on a thesis addressing a specific area of medical research, forming part of the university's broader higher degree by research offering of more than 180 PhD and Master of Philosophy programs across its disciplines.
b13910ee-4473-4920-a5e9-37adbb5a9c4d.curriculum: As a research-only doctorate, the Doctor of Philosophy (Medicine) has no coursework core or elective list. Admission requires an applicant to first secure a supervisory team within the relevant School and develop a formal Research Proposal describing the intended area of research, both submitted with the application. Candidature then proceeds through the standard stages of a University of Newcastle research degree: confirmation of candidature, ongoing supervised research, and submission and examination of a thesis, rather than enrolment in a set list of courses.
b13910ee-4473-4920-a5e9-37adbb5a9c4d.admission_requirements: An applicant for admission to the Doctoral Degree (Research), which includes the Doctor of Philosophy (Medicine), must have completed a Bachelor with Honours Class 1 or Honours Class II Division 1 (or an equivalent degree approved by the Head of School), or hold a Bachelor degree together with subsequent work and study recognised as equivalent to at least Honours Class II Division 1. In exceptional cases, other academic or professional qualifications and experience approved by the Head of School may be accepted, and in some disciplines a required minimum standard of professional experience may also satisfy admission. All applicants must also secure a supervisory team and submit a Research Proposal, Curriculum Vitae, and academic transcripts through the university's Graduate Research Application System.
b13910ee-4473-4920-a5e9-37adbb5a9c4d.english_requirements: Applicants must meet the University of Newcastle's English Language Proficiency Policy requirement for admission to a Doctoral Degree (Research) program, demonstrated through a recognised test such as IELTS or TOEFL, prior study taught and assessed in a recognised English-speaking country, or an equivalent accumulation of English through qualifications, work, or life experience, as set out in the university's English Language Proficiency Procedure.

f7ae6f8b-9bc6-475e-ab24-a85acec0a723._name: Doctor of Philosophy (Research) by Prior Publication (High Cost)
f7ae6f8b-9bc6-475e-ab24-a85acec0a723.description: The Doctor of Philosophy (Research) by Prior Publication lets an established researcher with a substantial body of peer-reviewed publications gain a University of Newcastle doctorate that recognises that existing body of work, rather than requiring a new thesis written from scratch. Applicants must not already hold a doctoral qualification. Admission is decided by a dedicated Admissions Assessment Panel that reviews the applicant's prior publications, thesis proposal, and academic referee report, and hears an oral presentation of the work, before recommending admission to the Dean of Graduate Research.
f7ae6f8b-9bc6-475e-ab24-a85acec0a723.curriculum: Rather than a taught curriculum, candidature is built around converting an existing set of publications into a single, integrated thesis. Applicants submit a thesis proposal listing the publications to be included, a statement of authorship, an account of how the research was developed, and a thematic overview showing how the individual publications form a coherent whole. The Admissions Assessment Panel, made up of the relevant Associate Dean (Research) or nominee, the School's HDR Convenor, and at least two senior academic staff in the discipline (plus an external assessor where needed), reviews this material, reads the prior publications, and holds an oral presentation and verbal defence with the applicant before recommending a decision, typically within around eight weeks of the School receiving the application.
f7ae6f8b-9bc6-475e-ab24-a85acec0a723.admission_requirements: Applicants must not have previously been awarded a doctoral level qualification. Before the Admissions Assessment Panel process, the Head of School or Deputy Head of School confirms the applicant meets the program's standard admission and selection criteria, based on the applicant's academic and professional standing and the viability of their proposed thesis. Applicants submit a Thesis Proposal, listing the publications for inclusion, a statement of authorship, and a thematic overview, plus an Academic Referee Report from someone familiar with the quality and significance of their prior publications, then attend an oral presentation and verbal defence before the Panel.
f7ae6f8b-9bc6-475e-ab24-a85acec0a723.english_requirements: Applicants must meet the University of Newcastle's English Language Proficiency Policy requirement for admission to a Doctoral Degree (Research) program, demonstrated through a recognised test such as IELTS or TOEFL, prior study taught and assessed in a recognised English-speaking country, or an equivalent accumulation of English through qualifications, work, or life experience, as set out in the university's English Language Proficiency Procedure.

d56c90d5-21a2-48f3-aa12-ebe60228cb55.description: The Master of Philosophy (Computer Science) is the University of Newcastle's research-only master's degree for candidates undertaking a supervised research project in computer science, run through the Graduate Research School alongside the university's PhD programs rather than as a coursework degree. Candidates work with a supervisory team within the relevant School on a thesis in an area of computer science research, forming part of the university's broader higher degree by research offering of more than 180 PhD and Master of Philosophy programs across its disciplines.
d56c90d5-21a2-48f3-aa12-ebe60228cb55.curriculum: As a research-only degree, the Master of Philosophy (Computer Science) has no coursework core or elective list. Admission requires an applicant to first secure a supervisory team within the relevant School and develop a formal Research Proposal describing the intended area of research, both submitted with the application. Candidature then proceeds through the standard stages of a University of Newcastle research degree: confirmation of candidature, ongoing supervised research, and submission and examination of a thesis, rather than enrolment in a set list of courses.
d56c90d5-21a2-48f3-aa12-ebe60228cb55.admission_requirements: An applicant for admission to the Master of Philosophy (Research), which includes the Master of Philosophy (Computer Science), must have completed a Bachelor with Honours Class 1 or Honours Class II Division 1, or another degree approved by the Head of School or Nominee, or in exceptional cases produce evidence of other academic or professional qualifications and experience approved by the Head of School. In some disciplines a required minimum standard of professional experience may also satisfy admission. All applicants must also secure a supervisory team and submit a Research Proposal, Curriculum Vitae, and academic transcripts through the university's Graduate Research Application System.
d56c90d5-21a2-48f3-aa12-ebe60228cb55.english_requirements: Applicants must meet the University of Newcastle's English Language Proficiency Policy requirement for admission to a Master of Philosophy (Research) program, demonstrated through a recognised test such as IELTS or TOEFL, prior study taught and assessed in a recognised English-speaking country, or an equivalent accumulation of English through qualifications, work, or life experience, as set out in the university's English Language Proficiency Procedure.

574b6150-cab4-4bde-8786-66cee23d136b.admission_requirements: Admission to the Master of Information Technology depends on an applicant's prior qualifications and, in some cases, industry experience. At AQF Level 7 entry: students with a three-year Bachelor degree in an unrelated field complete the 160-unit program (2 years full time or 4 years part time); students with a three-year Bachelor degree in an unrelated field plus at least two years of relevant senior-level industry experience study between 120 and 160 units depending on background; and students with a three-year Bachelor degree in a related field complete a 120-unit program (1.5 years full time or 3 years part time). At AQF Level 8 entry: students with a four-year Bachelor Honours degree in an unrelated field, a Graduate Certificate in an unrelated field, or a Graduate Diploma in an unrelated field study between 120 and 160 units depending on background; students with a Graduate Diploma in a related field complete a 120-unit program (1.5 years full time or 3 years part time); and students with a four-year Bachelor Honours degree in a related field complete an 80-unit program (1 year full time or 2 years part time). Related fields include information technology, computing, and technology; relevant senior-level experience includes roles such as senior analyst/programmer, senior developer, senior software engineer, senior business analyst, or IT manager.
574b6150-cab4-4bde-8786-66cee23d136b.english_requirements: Applicants need an IELTS overall score of 6.5 with no individual band below 6.0, or an equivalent recognised English test result.
